item.title: [LU-20049] e2fsck do not handle properly orphan files
item.description:

item.summary: e2fsck do not handle properly orphan files

status.description: The issue is open and ready for the assignee to start work on it.

comments.comment:
eaujames, these look like generic e2fsck issues, and not necessarily related to ldiskfs, so it would be good to (also) raise them on the linux-ext4 mailing list so they are fixed upstream.

In the second case (orphan inode with ea_inode), I expect that the kernel handles this properly, since it is just using the normal file deletion path, but file deletes in libext2fs do not handle the ea_inode properly?

Etienne Aujames, these look like generic e2fsck issues, and not necessarily related to ldiskfs, so it would be good to (also) raise them on the linux-ext4 mailing list so they are fixed upstream.

Yes. However, I will push the patch here first to be reviewed before send it upstream.

...libext2fs do not handle the ea_inode properly?

Not release_inode_blocks(), the function seems to be implemented with low-level functions (maybe old ones). So for example it does not support "well" bigalloc feature. I will try to use more upper level function to truncate orphan files (you can check remove_inode() from fuse2fs.c). There is no generic function to remove an inode. I think debugfs "rm" command have the same issue.

I would recommend to at least ask on linux-ext4 for suggestions on how to best fix the issue, even if you post the patch to Gerrit first for review. Having a high-level libext2fs function to delete an inode seems like a good idea, and I agree fuse2fs will certainly be interested in that.
